sections.h2: Ways to sell and move on in Davie
sections.html:
A Davie owner has three routes: hire an agent, sell without one, or take a cash purchase that leaves the repairs to the buyer. The work the house needs and how soon you need the money point to the right one.

The town looks and behaves differently from the beach cities to the east. Many lots have barns, fencing, pools or other outbuildings, and an inspector will flag those extras, so plan for them from the first day.

  • Agent: the biggest audience, plus showings, an appraisal and a loan contingency.
  • Owner sale: you draft the contract, give disclosures and coordinate closing.
  • Cash buyer: no lender, a common choice for inherited, rented or worn-out houses.

sections.h2: Western Theme rules and lot types
sections.html:
Davie describes itself as a ranching and western-lifestyle community with horse trails, an annual rodeo and a western-themed downtown, and it has more than 107,000 residents. The Town publishes a Western Theme Design Manual meant to preserve citrus, cattle, equestrian and rodeo heritage. Ask the Town whether it touches exterior work on your parcel, particularly inside the western-themed district.

Two sellers on opposite sides of town can face very different sales. A half-acre lot with an equestrian setup is priced and marketed differently from a townhome in a planned community. Sort out roof age, pool condition and outbuildings before showings begin.

If an association covers your property, request its governing documents early. In many communities a sale needs association approval, estoppel letters and a check for pending special assessments. A slow reply can hold up a closing longer than any repair.

Davie regulates short stays through a registration program. Under the Town Code (Chapter 16, Article IX) and section 509.242 of the Florida Statutes, a vacation rental is a unit rented to transient guests more than three times in a calendar year for periods under thirty days, or one advertised as regularly rented that way.

The Town requires a license from the state Department of Business and Professional Regulation before it accepts the application. The packet also asks for proof of ownership from the Broward County Property Appraiser, corporate documents if an entity owns the home, interior and exterior sketches, a Department of Revenue registration and a Broward tourist tax number.

Violations carry a civil penalty of up to $500 each. Call the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before you advertise.

sections.h2: Offices and records you will need
sections.html:
Three sources cover most of what a Davie seller needs. The Police Code Compliance Division, at 1230 South Nob Hill Road, handles vacation rental registration and code questions at 954-693-8237. The Broward County Property Appraiser's website, BCPA.net, is where the Town expects owners to pull proof of ownership. If an LLC or corporation holds title, the Town asks for corporate documents from Sunbiz.org.

Collect these before a buyer's attorney requests them. A clean ownership record, a current tax bill and written confirmation that no code case is open make a contract easier to sign.

A disabled veteran should keep one more item handy. The Town's rental program requires a DD214 and disability documentation to apply a veteran exemption, and the same paperwork helps if a buyer asks about the state's assessment reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers.

sections.h2: Broward property taxes and the sale
sections.html:
Broward County values and bills your Davie property on a state-set calendar: valuation on January 1, a proposed-tax notice in August and bills in November.

  • March 1 is the filing date for exemptions and classifications, which matters for a lot with an agricultural classification.
  • The clerk takes value petitions during the 25 days after the August notice.
  • Early payment discounts start at 4 percent in November and end at 1 percent in February.
  • Delinquency begins April 1.

Assessed value on non-homestead property can rise by at most 10 percent a year. Homesteads have the Save Our Homes cap instead, set at 3 percent or the inflation change, whichever is lower. That cap ends at sale, and the buyer begins at just value.

If part of your land holds an agricultural classification, ask the property appraiser how a sale or change in use affects it before you commit to a contract.

The Broward clerk records the deed, and Florida's stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. The statute counts any mortgage or encumbrance on the land, assumed or not, so paying off a loan does not shrink the base as sellers sometimes hope.

Every party shares liability for the tax whoever agrees to bear it. Your contract assigns the cost, and the title company usually collects it.

Recording fees come on top. Section 28.24 prices the first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, plus per-page records-fund and technology charges. Spousal homestead deeds and divorce deeds for the marital home carry listed exemptions, so ask the title agent before assuming tax applies.

Florida law gives each of these a defined path, and a sale stays possible.

When an heir sells, the Department of Revenue lists a personal representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable. Transfers made for estate planning are taxable, because no specific exemption covers them. Florida collects no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004.

After a foreclosure judgment the clerk's sale must fall 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to extend it. A buyer who closes sooner pays the lender and leaves the owner whatever equity remains.

Unpaid rent calls for a written three-day demand, not counting weekends and court holidays. A tenant raising any defense besides payment must deposit the rent with the court within five days or give up those defenses.

Order a payoff letter, confirm who holds the keys, and ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement a day or two ahead. Compare the statement with your contract so any difference is caught early. Take photo ID to the signing, and keep copies of what you sign.

faqs.q: Does Davie require registration for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town runs a vacation rental registration program tied to Chapter 16, Article IX of its code, and it asks for a state DBPR license first. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before advertising.

faqs.q: What is the Davie vacation rental fee?
faqs.a: A full registration year runs $500 and the half year from April 1 runs $300. Renewals cost $450 when the owner does not live there and $400 when the owner does.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a Davie property?
faqs.a: The Broward clerk records it and takes the deed stamp tax of 70 cents per $100, and the title company usually arranges both.

faqs.q: What happens to my property tax benefit when I sell in Davie?
faqs.a: The cap ends with the sale, and the buyer is assessed at just value the next January 1. Buying another Florida homestead? Ask the Broward appraiser about portability.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Davie house with tenants still living there?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer may accept the lease as written. For a vacant house, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and only a sheriff can physically remove an occupant.
